correctness.rationale: The proof starts from Verra's displayed product for D(g) and his theorem deg(gamma)=D(g)+2^(g-3). Exact factorial cancellation gives the recurrence D(g+1)/D(g)=4(2g-3)/g with D(3)=1; 2^(g-3) C_(g-2) has the same recurrence and initial value. Legendre's formula gives v_2(C_m)=s_2(m+1)-1, so only m+1 a power of two can make C_m+1 even. For m=2^r-1 an explicit odd-factorial induction gives C_m=1 mod 4, making the extra valuation exactly one. The bundled checker reconstructs the original product from the actual package path and verifies all identities through g=300.

value.rationale: The Gauss-map degree is a central enumerative invariant of a theta divisor and is used to stratify moduli of principally polarized abelian varieties. The theorem turns the generic Prym formula from a classical product involving symmetric rank loci into a single Catalan number, making growth and arithmetic transparent. The exact dyadic law then isolates a natural sparse phase at genera one above powers of two, where the normalized Gauss degree is exactly 2 modulo 4. This is a structural simplification and complete arithmetic classification of a canonical geometric degree.
